story.title: Bernie Sanders proposes banning ‘superintelligence’ and putting violators in prison

facts.text: Greg Casar, are unveiling legislation Wednesday that would ban artificial superintelligence and create a federal agency to oversee advanced AI as some of the industry’s own leaders urge Congress to impose guardrails on the advancing technology.
The bill, provided first to the Associated Press, would also pause advanced AI development until guidelines are implemented while creating the Department of Artificial Intelligence.

The legislation would permanently prohibit artificial superintelligence, which it defines as a system that exceeds human cognitive ability or has sufficient capabilities to plan and execute the destruction or disempowerment of humanity.

Juan Felipe Cerón Uribe, a researcher in OpenAI’s Safety Systems, said in a statement supporting the bill that “superintelligence could either go extremely right or extremely wrong” and that “we shouldn’t be playing such games.” Swante Scholz, a software engineer at Google DeepMind who said he was not speaking on behalf of his employer, said on the current path of development, the “most likely outcome is an existential catastrophe for humanity.” “A ban on superintelligence development would be a positive change for the foreseeable future,” Scholz said in a statement.

On Tuesday, Trump told the United Nations General Assembly that artificial intelligence will be renamed “super intelligence." “I think Trump has very little understanding of what this issue is about,” Sanders said.
The bill from Sanders and Casar faces long odds in the Republican-controlled Congress, where lawmakers have struggled to coalesce around even less sweeping AI regulations.
Under the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, AI leaders would face up to 20 years in prison for violating the law.

Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Greg Casar introduced the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act on September 3, 2026, a bill that would permanently ban the development of artificial superintelligence in the United States and temporarily pause research on frontier models.
Violators face up to twenty years in prison, and companies that break the law face forced dissolution.

"Almost every day, there's a frightening new story about how Big Tech companies are losing control of the technology they're developing, with potentially catastrophic results," said Sanders in a statement announcing the bill.

Neither framework would change automatically if this bill became law, but a US ban on superintelligence would still reshape what UK and EU users and developers can access, since the supply comes largely from American labs.
Bernie Sanders, one of the most vocal opponents of unregulated AI and the race toward superintelligence, has announced the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act alongside Rep.
That's similar to the penalty for unlawfully developing nuclear weapons.
The penalties section makes it clear that violators face more than a slap on the wrist.
"Entities shall be subject to the corporate death penalty, and persons shall be subject to not more than 20 years in prison," it warns.
